questions.question: In Shakespeare's 'Julius Caesar', who delivers the impassioned funeral oration beginning 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'?
questions.explanation: Mark Antony sways the Roman plebeians against the conspirators in Act 3 Scene 2.

questions.question: In 'Macbeth', which nobleman cries out 'What, all my pretty chickens and their dam / At one fell swoop?' upon hearing of his slaughtered family?
questions.explanation: Macduff receives the tragic news of his castle slaughter in Act 4 Scene 3 in England.

questions.question: Which romantic comedy by William Shakespeare centers on the witty skirmishes and reluctant love between Beatrice and Benedick?
questions.explanation: Beatrice and Benedick engage in a merry war of wits in Messina in Much Ado About Nothing.

questions.question: Convert into indirect speech: He said to me, 'What are you doing here today?'
options: He asked to me what was I doing there that day.
He asked me what I was doing there that day.
He inquired of me what I am doing there today.
He asked me that what was I doing here today.
questions.explanation: In indirect wh-questions, today becomes that day, here becomes there, and word order is assertive.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: The venerable monk said to the child, 'May God bless you with wisdom!'
options: The venerable monk prayed that God might bless the child with wisdom.
The venerable monk said that may God bless the child with wisdom.
The venerable monk exclaimed that God should bless the child with wisdom.
The venerable monk wished the child that God will bless him with wisdom.
questions.explanation: Optative sentences expressing blessings are converted using prayed or blessed with might.

questions.question: Which 1593 narrative poem composed in six-line stanzas was Shakespeare's first published work, dedicated to Henry Wriothesley, Earl of Southampton?
questions.explanation: Venus and Adonis was published in 1593 while the London theatres were closed due to the plague.

questions.question: Which distinguished Shakespearean scholar authored the monumental critical study 'Shakespearean Tragedy' in 1904?
questions.explanation: A.C. Bradley lectures analyzed the character psychology of Shakespeare four principal tragedies.

questions.question: Which 1821 lyrical drama by P.B. Shelley was inspired by the contemporary Greek War of Independence and concludes with 'The world's great age begins anew'?
questions.explanation: Hellas was Shelley passionate lyrical celebration of Greece struggle against Ottoman Turkish rule.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form: The father said to his son, 'Do not waste your precious time.'
options: The father advised his son not to waste his precious time.
The father forbade his son not to waste his precious time.
The father said his son that he do not waste his time.
The father requested his son do not waste your precious time.
questions.explanation: Negative imperatives with Do not convert to advised or urged followed by not to infinitive.

questions.question: What is the exact antonym of the word 'AUDACIOUS'?
questions.explanation: Audacious means showing a willingness to take bold risks; its opposite is timid or fearful.

questions.question: 'Swiftly walk o'er the western wave, / Spirit of Night!' is the invocation opening which famous lyric by P.B. Shelley?
options: Lines: When the Lamp Is Shattered
questions.explanation: To Night composed in 1821 personifies the spirit of night arriving across the western sky.

questions.question: In 'A Defence of Poetry', to which musical instrument whose strings vibrate when touched by the wind does Shelley compare the human mind?
questions.explanation: Shelley writes that man is an instrument over which a series of external and internal impressions pass like wind over an Aeolian lyre.

questions.question: 'O soft embalmer of the still midnight, / Shutting, with careful fingers and benign' is the invocation in which sonnet by John Keats?
options: On First Looking into Chapman's Homer
questions.explanation: Keats sonnet To Sleep appeals to sleep to seal the curious eyes from daylight cares.

questions.question: Select the closest synonym for the word 'ZEALOUS':
questions.explanation: Zealous means having or showing great energy or enthusiasm, synonymous with ardent.

questions.question: What is the antonym of the adjective 'TRANSIENT'?
questions.explanation: Transient means lasting only for a short time; its opposite is permanent or enduring.

questions.question: Which unfinished epic poem by John Keats, composed in heroic blank verse, chronicles the fall of the Titans before the Olympian god Apollo?
options: The Fall of Hyperion: A Dream
questions.explanation: Hyperion was Keats attempt at a Miltonic blank verse epic on the triumph of Apollo.

questions.question: Which essayist, editor of 'The Examiner', and friend of John Keats famously championed Keats, Shelley, and Byron in his Cockney School articles?
questions.explanation: Leigh Hunt published Keats first sonnet O Solitude in The Examiner and fostered his literary circle.

questions.question: In Alfred Lord Tennyson's dramatic monologue 'Tithonus', what tragic fate does Tithonus lament after being granted immortality by Aurora without eternal youth?
options: Turned to cold stone on the seashore
Condemned to sail forever on stormy seas
Withered slowly in the arms of immortal youth
Lost all human memory of earthly existence
questions.explanation: Tithonus laments his cruel immortality while aging perpetually beside the youthful goddess of dawn.

questions.question: Choose the correct synonym of the word 'LACONIC':
questions.explanation: Laconic means using very few words, matching terse or concise.

questions.question: What is the antonym of the noun 'DESPAIR'?
questions.explanation: Despair is the complete loss or absence of hope; hope is its exact antonym.

questions.question: Which sixteen-line poem did Alfred Lord Tennyson request should always be printed as the final poem in every edition of his collected works?
questions.explanation: Written in 1889, Crossing the Bar expresses Tennyson tranquil contemplation of his impending death.

questions.question: Stephen Blackpool, an honest factory weaver who refuses to join a union and is ostracized, is a central figure in which Dickens novel?
questions.explanation: Stephen Blackpool tragedy in Coketown illustrates the harsh human costs of industrialization.

questions.question: Which of the following was Charles Dickens's final novel, left uncompleted at six chapters at his death in June 1870?
questions.explanation: Dickens died of a stroke in 1870 leaving the resolution of Edwin Drood disappearance a mystery.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly distinguishes between 'LOATH' and 'LOATHE':
options: He was loathe to admit that he loathed dishonesty.
He was loathed to admit that he loath dishonesty.
He loath the sight and was loathe to stay.
He was loath to admit that he loathed dishonesty.
questions.explanation: Loath without e is an adjective meaning reluctant; loathe with e is a verb meaning to detest.

questions.question: A person who eats human flesh is referred to as a:
questions.explanation: A cannibal is an individual who consumes the flesh of other human beings.

questions.question: 'Our birth is but a sleep and a forgetting: / The Soul that rises with us, our life's Star' occurs in which celebrated ode by William Wordsworth?
questions.explanation: This stanza asserts the Platonic doctrine of anamnesis or pre-existence of the human soul.

questions.question: In Book I of 'The Prelude', which nocturnal escapade leads the young Wordsworth to be terrified by a huge black peak towering in the darkness?
options: Hunting birds across the stormy fells
Stealing a small rowing boat on the lake
Climbing to an eagle nest on the crag
Skating late at night across frozen ice
questions.explanation: Wordsworth recounts taking a shepherd boat on Ullswater and watching a black crag loom up.

questions.question: 'A slumber did my spirit seal; / I had no human fears' is the opening of which two-stanza poem from Wordsworth's famous group of lyrics?
questions.explanation: A slumber did my spirit seal is one of the five enigmatic Lucy poems composed in 1798-1799.

questions.question: A state or system of government ruled by a single monarch is known as a:
questions.explanation: A monarchy is a form of government with a monarch at the head.

questions.question: Something that is incapable of being seen through because it prevents light from passing is:
questions.explanation: Opaque objects do not let light pass through; transparent objects allow light completely.

questions.question: 'Teach us to care and not to care / Teach us to sit still' is a repeated prayer in which 1930 poem by T.S. Eliot celebrating his conversion to Anglicanism?
questions.explanation: Ash-Wednesday records Eliot difficult spiritual journey from despair to Christian faith.

questions.question: Which 1939 verse drama by T.S. Eliot, drawing upon Aeschylus's 'Oresteia', explores Harry Monchensey's pursuit by the spectral Eumenides?
questions.explanation: The Family Reunion deals with inherited family curses and Christian expiation at Wishwood.

questions.question: In which personal essay does Charles Lamb celebrate the elderly lawyers, cloistered courts, and fountain of the legal inns of London?
options: Christ's Hospital Five and Thirty Years Ago
The Old Benchers of the Inner Temple
questions.explanation: Lamb was born in the Inner Temple and pays affectionate tribute to its old benchers.

questions.question: The scientific study of the history and origins of words is called:
questions.explanation: Etymology is the study of word origins; entomology is the study of insects.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to read between the lines'?
options: To read a book carefully from beginning to end
To skip uninteresting paragraphs in a novel
To understand the hidden or implied meaning
To underline important sentences in red ink
questions.explanation: It refers to discovering implicit meaning that is not directly stated in the text.

questions.question: In which essay of Elia does Charles Lamb playfully designate calendars, pocket books, and chess manuals as 'books which are no books' (biblia a-biblia)?
options: Detached Thoughts on Books and Reading
questions.explanation: Lamb classifies utilitarian reference publications as biblia a-biblia lacking true soul.

questions.question: Giles Winterborne and Marty South are loyal woodland characters in which pastoral Wessex novel by Thomas Hardy?
questions.explanation: The Woodlanders in 1887 portrays tragic love against the orchards and woods of Little Hintock.

questions.question: What is the title of Thomas Hardy's epic blank-verse closet drama in three parts and nineteen acts depicting the Napoleonic War era?
questions.explanation: The Dynasts published between 1904 and 1908 presents Europe history controlled by the Immanent Will.

questions.question: The idiomatic expression 'to cry over spilt milk' means:
options: To complain about the poor quality of dairy foods
To weep loudly during an unexpected disaster
To clean a messy kitchen floor after an accident
To lament uselessly over an error that cannot be rectified
questions.explanation: It signifies wasting time grieving over past losses that cannot be undone.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to turn a deaf ear'?
options: To whisper secrets quietly to a friend
To suffer from medical deafness in one ear
To disregard or deliberately refuse to listen
questions.explanation: It means deliberately ignoring advice, warnings, or appeals.

questions.question: 'Home is the place where, when you have to go there, / They have to take you in' is spoken by Warren in which Robert Frost dramatic dialogue poem?
options: The Death of the Hired Man
questions.explanation: Mary and Warren converse about the aging wanderer Silas in The Death of the Hired Man in 1914.

questions.question: 'My long two-pointed ladder's sticking through a tree / Toward heaven still' opens which meditative agricultural poem by Robert Frost?
questions.explanation: After Apple-Picking explores exhaustion, sleep, and the burdens of harvest in North of Boston.

questions.question: In Kamala Das's frank confessional poem 'The Looking Glass', what ultimate advice is offered regarding what a woman should surrender in love?
options: Gift him all that makes you woman
Remain silent during moments of passion
Guard your heart with sovereign pride
questions.explanation: The poem explores raw female desire urging a woman to gift him all that makes you woman.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: The company complied ______ all environmental regulations.
questions.explanation: The verb comply is standardly followed by the preposition with.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Beware ______ pickpockets in crowded public gatherings.
questions.explanation: The cautionary verb beware takes the preposition of.

questions.question: In which novel by Mulk Raj Anand is the peasant protagonist Lalu shipped across the black waters to fight in French trenches during the First World War?
questions.explanation: Across the Black Waters published in 1940 depicts Indian sepoy experiences in European warfare.

questions.question: Robert Jordan, an idealistic American volunteer tasked with blowing up a mountain bridge in Spain, is the protagonist of which novel by Ernest Hemingway?
questions.explanation: For Whom the Bell Tolls published in 1940 is set during the Spanish Civil War.

questions.question: In which autobiographical poem does Nissim Ezekiel chronicle his Jewish ancestry, London student years, and return to Bombay as an Indian poet?
questions.explanation: Background, Casually traces Ezekiel journey from a Roman Catholic school in Bombay to London and back.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: In view of his long service, the committee dispensed ______ the formal test.
questions.explanation: Dispense with means to manage without or forgo a requirement.

questions.question: Which prefix can be attached to 'REPLACEABLE' to denote that an item cannot be replaced?
questions.explanation: Words starting with r take the negative prefix ir- to form irreplaceable.

questions.question: Walt Whitman's opening autobiographical poem in 'Leaves of Grass' celebrating his Long Island birthplace is titled:
questions.explanation: Paumanok was the Native American name for Long Island where Whitman was born in 1819.

questions.question: Which 1932 novel by William Faulkner interweaves the tragic fate of the racially divided outcast Joe Christmas with the pregnant Lena Grove?
questions.explanation: Light in August explores racial identity, religion, and community violence in Yoknapatawpha County.

questions.question: Which dream-allegory poem by Geoffrey Chaucer depicts birds gathering on Saint Valentine's Day before Dame Nature to choose their mates?
questions.explanation: The Parliament of Fowls introduces the tradition of Valentine Day as a celebration for lovers.

questions.question: Which suffix is attached to the noun 'LEADER' to form an abstract noun indicating the office of leading?
questions.explanation: Leader takes the suffix -ship to form leadership.

questions.question: What is the correct negative prefix for the adjective 'LITERATE'?
questions.explanation: Words starting with l like literate take il- to form illiterate.

questions.question: In 'The Canterbury Tales', which drunken pilgrim insists on telling a raucous fabliau about Nicholas and Alison right after the Knight's noble tale?
questions.explanation: The Miller interrupts the Host to tell a comic fabliau mocking an old carpenter.

questions.question: Which 1866 novel by George Eliot concerns political reform and Radicalism surrounding the 1832 Reform Bill in Treby Magna?
questions.explanation: Felix Holt centers on elections, trade union ideals, and an inheritance mystery.

questions.question: What was the collective title of George Eliot's first published fictional series containing 'The Sad Fortunes of the Rev. Amos Barton'?
questions.explanation: Scenes of Clerical Life published in Blackwood Magazine in 1857 was her fiction debut.

questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence regarding subject-verb concord:
options: The quality of these mangoes were exceptional.
The quality of these mangoes is exceptional.
The quality of these mangoes have been exceptional.
The quality of these mangoes are exceptional.
questions.explanation: The grammatical subject is the singular noun quality, requiring the singular verb is.

questions.question: Transform the simple sentence into a compound sentence: 'In spite of his severe poverty, he remained honest.'
options: Because he was poor, he remained honest.
Being severely poor, he remained honest.
Although he was poor, he remained honest.
He was severely poor, yet he remained honest.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence connects two independent clauses using a coordinating conjunction like yet.

questions.question: Which 1964 one-act drama by Arthur Miller takes place in a detention room in occupied France where men await Nazi racial inspection?
questions.explanation: Incident at Vichy examines complicity, guilt, and the psychology of anti-Semitic persecution.

questions.question: In Arthur Miller's 'All My Sons', which of Joe Keller's sons killed himself during the war out of shame after hearing of his father's defective cylinder heads?
questions.explanation: Larry letter to Ann reveals that he deliberately crashed his plane out of grief over his father crime.

questions.question: Which 1981 novel by Toni Morrison follows the love affair between Jadine Childs and the fugitive Son on the Caribbean island of Isle des Chevaliers?
questions.explanation: Tar Baby explores cultural identity and black heritage in a Caribbean setting.

questions.question: Transform the comparative degree into positive degree: 'Lead is heavier than any other metal.'
options: No other metal is as heavy as lead.
Lead is as heavy as other metals.
No other metal is heavier than lead.
Lead is the heaviest of all metals.
questions.explanation: Comparative heavier than any other metal transforms into positive No other metal is as heavy as.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct subjunctive sentence:
options: He walked as though he were lame.
He walked as though he is lame.
He walked as though he would be lame.
He walked as though he was lame.
questions.explanation: Clauses introduced by as though or as if expressing hypothetical situations take were.

questions.question: Which 2008 historical novel by Toni Morrison, set in seventeenth-century colonial America, recounts the story of an orphaned slave girl named Florens?
questions.explanation: A Mercy examines the early beginnings of the American slave trade before racial lines solidified.

questions.question: 'To err is human, to forgive divine' in Alexander Pope's 'An Essay on Criticism' is a classic example of which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: Antithesis balances two opposing thoughts against each other in parallel grammatical phrases.

questions.question: Using the expression 'the White House' to refer to the executive administration of the United States is an example of:
questions.explanation: Metonymy substitutes the name of an attribute or closely associated object for the thing meant.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences exhibits correct subject-verb agreement with 'Either... or'?
options: Either you or he were mistaken.
Either you or he is mistaken.
Either you or he are mistaken.
Either you or he have been mistaken.
questions.explanation: In either... or constructions, the verb agrees with the nearer subject he.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They manufacture fine leather shoes in this industrial factory.'
options: Fine leather shoes have manufactured in this industrial factory.
Fine leather shoes are manufactured in this industrial factory.
Fine leather shoes were manufactured in this industrial factory.
Fine leather shoes are being manufactured in this factory.
questions.explanation: Simple present active manufacture becomes simple present passive are manufactured.

questions.question: 'Why then, O brawling love! O loving hate!' spoken by Romeo in Act 1 of 'Romeo and Juliet' features a series of which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: Romeo contrasts his confused romantic feelings through paired contradictory terms.

questions.question: 'The gray-eyed morn smiles on the frowning night' in Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Attributing human actions like smiling and frowning to morning and night is personification.

questions.question: Expressing that an action was commendable by stating 'His efforts were not unpraiseworthy' illustrates which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: Litotes uses a double negative or negation of the opposite to convey an understated affirmative.

questions.question: Change the passive sentence into active voice: 'A melodious hymn was sung by the cathedral choir.'
options: The cathedral choir was singing a melodious hymn.
The cathedral choir sang a melodious hymn.
The cathedral choir sings a melodious hymn.
The cathedral choir had sung a melodious hymn.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive was sung transforms into simple past active sang.

questions.question: Select the sentence with correct inversion following the negative adverb 'Seldom':
options: Seldom I have witnessed such profound artistic brilliance.
Seldom I witnessed such profound artistic brilliance.
Seldom did I witnessed such profound artistic brilliance.
Seldom have I witnessed such profound artistic brilliance.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbs like seldom at the start of a sentence require auxiliary inversion.

questions.question: Which 1589 Elizabethan rhetorical treatise, attributed to George Puttenham, provides an extensive systematic classification of poetic forms and figures?
questions.explanation: Puttenham handbook analyzed the craft and courtly decorum of English poetry in three books.

questions.question: In 'An Essay of Dramatic Poesy' (1668), John Dryden presented four speakers discussing drama; which speaker represented Dryden's own view?
questions.explanation: Neander meaning new man defended modern English drama and Shakespeare against French models.

questions.question: Which foundational New Critical work was published by William Empson in 1930, demonstrating seven distinct types of verbal ambiguity in poetry?
questions.explanation: Empson landmark work explored how poetic language generates multiple concurrent meanings.

questions.question: Which of the following options represents the correct spelling of the word denoting playful naughtiness?
questions.explanation: Mischievous is three syllables and spelled m-i-s-c-h-i-e-v-o-u-s without an i after v.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling of the word denoting close observation or guarding:
questions.explanation: Surveillance is spelled with double l and ending ance as s-u-r-v-e-i-l-l-a-n-c-e.

questions.question: In Aristotle's 'Poetics', which term designates the fatal flaw or tragic misjudgment that causes the downfall of a noble protagonist?
questions.explanation: Hamartia is the tragic error of judgment or character flaw leading to catastrophe.

questions.question: The Oxford Movement within the Victorian Church of England was alternatively named the Tractarian Movement because of their publication:
questions.explanation: Newman, Keble, and Pusey published ninety Tracts for the Times defending Anglican apostolic tradition.

questions.question: The Caroline era of English literature corresponds to the reign of which English monarch between 1625 and 1649?
questions.explanation: Caroline is derived from Carolus, the Latin form of Charles, denoting Charles I reign.

questions.question: Which of the following displays the correct spelling of the word denoting the study of antiquities?
questions.explanation: Archaeology preserves the classic diphthong ae as a-r-c-h-a-e-o-l-o-g-y.

questions.question: Find the correctly spelled word denoting an author of plays:
questions.explanation: Playwright is spelled with wright meaning a maker or crafter, not write.

questions.question: Which satirical term was coined by W.E. Aytoun in 1854 to mock the hyperbolic and melodramatic style of poets like Sydney Dobell and Alexander Smith?
questions.explanation: The Spasmodic School was criticized for emotional self-indulgence and bombastic imagery.

questions.question: What is the traditional name for the seven-line stanza rhyming 'ababbcc', named after King James I of Scotland who used it in 'The Kingis Quair'?
questions.explanation: Rime royale was adopted by Chaucer and popularized by King James I of Scotland.

questions.question: A medieval and early Tudor allegorical drama in which virtues and vices struggle for the soul of Mankind or Everyman is called a:
questions.explanation: Morality plays like Everyman dramatized moral lessons with allegorical personifications.

questions.question: Select the sentence with correct semicolon punctuation between independent clauses:
options: To err is human, to forgive is divine.
To err is human; and to forgive is divine.
To err is human; to forgive is divine.
To err is human: to forgive is divine.
questions.explanation: A semicolon appropriately links two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction.

questions.question: Identify the grammatical tense in: 'By five o'clock this evening, he will have completed the entire assignment.'
questions.explanation: Will have completed is future perfect tense indicating completion by a future point.
